qs.q: During the inspection phase of a cardiovascular examination, a prominent pulsation is observed in the left parasternal region. What does this finding most likely indicate?
o: Left ventricular volume overload and dilation
Aortic root aneurysm with secondary dissection
Severe mitral regurgitation with left atrial strain
Pericardial effusion with acute cardiac tamponade
qs.e: A parasternal heave or pulsation is a classic physical sign associated with right ventricular hypertrophy.

qs.q: During a cardiovascular examination, a fourth heart sound S4 is auscultated in an elderly hypertensive patient. What mechanical event produces this extra heart sound?
o: Atrial contraction against a stiffened ventricle.
Rapid ventricular filling during early diastole.
Closure of the mitral valve under high pressure.
Opening of the aortic valve at systole start.
Turbulent flow across a calcified aortic valve.
qs.e: An S4 sound is produced by forceful atrial contraction pushing blood into a stiff, non-compliant left ventricle.
